what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat cystic fibrosis (CF) in patients aged 2 years and older who have at least one copy of the F508del gene mutation, or other mutations that respond to this treatment. It works by helping the CFTR protein in your body work better, which improves lung function, reduces flare-ups, and can help you feel better overall.
how_to_take: Take the morning dose (2 elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor tablets) and the evening dose (1 ivacaftor tablet) with a fat-containing food, such as eggs, butter, peanut butter, cheese pizza, or whole-milk dairy products like whole milk or yogurt. This helps your body absorb the medicine properly. Swallow the tablets whole — do not crush, chew, or break them. For young children, granules may be mixed with 1 teaspoon of soft food or liquid. Take doses approximately 12 hours apart (for example, 8 AM and 8 PM).
dosing: Adults and children 6 years and older: Take 2 elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor tablets in the MORNING and 1 ivacaftor tablet in the EVENING, about 12 hours later. Children ages 2 to 5 years: Dosing is based on body weight and comes in granule packets — your doctor or pharmacist will tell you exactly how many packets to give. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as doses may be adjusted for liver problems or drug interactions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose and it has been less than 6 hours since it was due, take it as soon as you remember with a fat-containing food. If it has been MORE than 6 hours, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular scheduled time. Do NOT double up doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep tablets in their original packaging and away from moisture and heat. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep this medicine out of reach of children. If using granule packets for young children, once mixed with food or liquid, give the dose right away and do not save any leftovers.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, Seville oranges (often found in marmalades), and starfruit — these can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid St. John's Wort (an herbal supplement), as it can make this medicine less effective. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because many drugs can interact with this medication, including certain antibiotics, antifungals, seizure medicines, and HIV medications.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes, dark or tea-colored urine, stomach pain, nausea, or vomiting (signs of liver problems); changes in your vision or eye pain (eye problems have been seen in children); rash, hives, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing (signs of an allergic reaction); abnormal menstrual periods or unusual hormone changes; or if you feel generally unwell or notice any unusual symptoms. Also contact your doctor before starting or stopping any other medications.
when_it_works: Many patients notice improvements in how they feel — such as easier breathing — within a few weeks of starting treatment. Lung function tests (FEV1) may improve within 4 weeks. However, it may take longer to notice the full benefit. This medication works best when taken consistently every day as prescribed. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel better.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Talk to your doctor before taking this medicine if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The effects on an unborn baby or nursing infant are not fully known. Liver Disease: If you have moderate or severe liver disease, your doctor may lower your dose or monitor you more closely. Kidney Disease: No dose adjustment is usually needed for kidney disease, but tell your doctor about any kidney problems. Children ages 2 to 5: This medicine is available as granule packets for young children. Carefully follow the weight-based dosing instructions provided by your doctor or pharmacist.
